title: Chapter 4 Quiz 7
description: Rows and columns: arrays with two indexes.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: What is a **two-dimensional array**?
options: A pair of two named arrays
A table of rows and columns
questions.explanation: It uses two indexes: row and column. Watch out: it is one structure, not two separate arrays.

questions.question: Which Pascal declaration creates a 2×2 array of integers?
questions.explanation: One range per dimension, separated by a comma. Watch out: array[1..4] has four cells but only one index.

questions.question: How many cells does an array [1..3, 1..4] have?
questions.explanation: 3 rows × 4 columns = 12. Watch out: the cells are multiplied, not added (3 + 4 = 7).

questions.question: M is the matrix [1 2 3 / 4 5 6 / 7 8 9] (row, column). Give each value.
questions.explanation: M[row, column]. Watch out: M[2,3] is row 2, column 3 (6), and M[3,2] is row 3, column 2 (8).

questions.question: What is the sum of all the values of the matrix above?
How do we visit every cell of a 2D array?
questions.explanation: One loop for the rows, one inside it for the columns.

questions.question: Complete the algorithm that sums a 3×3 matrix.
questions.code:
sum ← 0
For i From 0 To 2
    For j From {{1}} To 2
        Read(matrix[i][j])
        sum ← sum + {{2}}
    EndFor
EndFor
Display(sum)
questions.explanation: The inner loop starts at 0, like the outer one, and adds the cell just read.

questions.question:
How many times does the inner body run?
```
For i From 1 To 3 Do
    For j From 1 To i Do
        Display(i, j)
    EndFor
EndFor
```
questions.explanation: i = 1 gives 1 pass, i = 2 gives 2, i = 3 gives 3: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6. Watch out: the inner loop depends on i, so it is not 3 × 3 = 9.

questions.question: This should add every cell of a 3×3 matrix. One line is wrong. Find it and choose the fix.
questions.code:
Let sum ← 0
For i From 1 To 3 Do
    For j From 1 To 3 Do
        sum ← sum + M[i][i]
    EndFor
EndFor
questions.explanation: Each cell is M[i][j]. Watch out: M[i][i] adds only the diagonal cells, and each of them three times.
